scope: Behavior, ARIA, parts, events, focus and state attributes of the web component in happy-dom (node:test), and the React renderer's server markup and client state. Placement, rendered lengths and motion are covered by the browser geometry check and the React parity check; visual quality and screen-reader output are not certified.

checks.covers: preset and parts anatomy, trigger and dialog ARIA, openchange (cancelable; trigger-press, escape-key, outside-press, close-press, trigger-hover), focus moves in and returns, modal trap, open / default-open / disabled, no native form elements
resolvePopup: 1u offset, 2u × 1u arrow, card-sm padding and radius, group gap, width cap; arrowOffset centering and clamping
React SSR: the same data-* and recipe classes as the web component on host and parts, the composed parts render the preset's markup, render and className functions

limitations: Placement (CSS anchor positioning or the script positioner), the top layer and the reveal motion need a real browser; unit tests cover the attributes they key on.
React styling parity is checked in the browser: apps/studio/react-check.html ("fails": []).
modal traps focus but does not lock page scroll or make the page inert (Base UI modal also does both).

Geometry review, manual items (2026-11-02, studio Chromium at u = 3, 4, the theme unit 4.5 and 6, light and dark): growth (long content wraps at the 80u cap and the popup grows; past the space beside the trigger it scrolls inside the positioner, the arrow outside it), RTL (the CSS anchor rule uses logical position-area spans, so start / end mirror; the arrow offset is measured from the boxes; the script fallback aligns physically), focus (the trigger keeps its 2px ring without changing size; a popup with no tabbable child takes focus itself, tabindex=-1), screenshots of the Popups family and the size ladder checked light and dark.
